chain.description: During startup of standby reboiler EA-425B, opening quench-water valves (proc:P-REB-START-2:early) while shell-side block valves HV-B-SIN and HV-B-SOUT remain closed traps heat in the shell; pressure rises above 2068 kPa with no relief path (RV-PATH-EA425B needs those same valves open), leading to tube rupture (m:S-EA-425B:as_well_as:composition) that互
chain.reason: proc:P-REB-START-2:early creates heat input to an isolated shell; plant facts show quench-water valves normally closed (HV-QW-B-IN.normal_position, HV-QW-B-OUT.normal_position), process valves normally closed (HV-B-SIN.normal_position, HV-B-SOUT.normal_position), relief path blocked (RV-PATH-EA425B.inlet_valve_ids), and design pressure 2068 kPa (EA-425B.design_pressure_kpa). This combination makes tube rupture (m:S-EA-425B:as_well_as:composition) credible.

chain.severity_reason: Tube rupture in EA-425B releases flammable hydrocarbons (propane, propylene, C4-heavies) to occupied outdoor Olefins unit (LOC-OLEFINS-UNIT), causing significant release with potential fire/explosion leading to single fatality or serious injuries on site.

layers.reason: does not apply: Scenario states pressure rises with no relief path because RV-PATH-EA425B requires inlet valves HV-B-SIN/HV-B-SOUT open; relief device cannot relieve overpressure when isolated from equipment.

evidence.summary: Blocked-in heating check: if EA-425B is isolated while hot quench water stays on, vapour pressure reaches at least 1.6× design (lowest of the listed chemicals: PROPANE)
flags: pure-component vapour pressure; liquid-full thermal expansion not modelled; real pressure can be higher
no data: C4-HEAVIES; bound covers listed chemicals only

recommendations.action: Add an interlock on HV-QW-B-IN and HV-QW-B-OUT that prevents opening unless HV-B-SIN and HV-B-SOUT are both confirmed open.
recommendations.reason: The scenario occurs when quench water valves open early per proc:P-REB-START-2 while shell-side block valves remain closed, isolating the relief path. An engineered interlock directly prevents the out-of-sequence operation that defeats RV-PATH-EA425B, preferred over procedure revision alone.
